VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The core soft-match / identity-key redesign is placed well: `Soundex` is correctly a reusable `util` class (the same package as `E164Telephone`) and is shared cleanly by both `Owner.getIdentityKey()` and `ClinicServiceImpl.applySoftMatch`; `applySoftMatch` sits naturally next to `assertIdentityUnique`/`assignHouseholdId` in the service and is wired into the save path in an obvious spot. One structural issue, though:

**Duplicated SHA-256→hex logic across two classes.** The new `Owner.sha256LowerHex(String)` (`Owner.java:428`) is a near-copy of the pre-existing `ClinicServiceImpl.sha256UpperHex(String, int)` (`ClinicServiceImpl.java:408`): same `MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256")`, same UTF-8 digest, same per-byte `String.format("%02x"/"%02X")` loop, same `NoSuchAlgorithmException → IllegalStateException("SHA-256 not available")` handling. The only differences are hex case and truncation length. This is exactly the kind of pure derivation helper the codebase already factors into the `util` package — and this very change demonstrates that pattern by adding `Soundex` there. Adding a second private copy inside the JPA entity instead misses that established convention and puts low-level crypto/hashing plumbing (`MessageDigest`, checked-exception wrapping, hex formatting) into the domain model.

Suggested fix: extract a small shared helper in `util` (e.g. `Sha256Hex` / `HexDigest` with `lowerHex(value)` and `upperHex(value, chars)`, or a single `hex(value)` the callers slice/upper-case) and have both `Owner.getIdentityKey()` and `ClinicServiceImpl.generateHouseholdId`/`sha256UpperHex` delegate to it. That removes the duplication and keeps the hashing plumbing out of the entity, consistent with how `Soundex` and `E164Telephone` are handled.
